characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: load cell and strain gauge (a precision extensometer was also developed by the authors for the earlier large-deformation measurement of SPCE)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Species D (Heat-treated after received) gives elastic modulus 189 for the strain region 0–0.05% and 189 for the whole elastic range, i.e. essentially unchanged between the two strain regions, unlike A, B and C which show a gap between the two ranges.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: stress–strain curve measured up to ~1% strain; elastic modulus obtained from the stress–strain curves within the elastic deformation region (Fig. 4); SPCC sheet of 1.2 mm thickness
characterization_methods.purpose: to confirm the effect of movable dislocations by comparing specimen conditions A–E, and to measure the elastic modulus of the heat-treated (D) specimen before/after the 373 K/90 h heat treatment
characterization_methods.technique: tensile test (stress–strain measurement with strain gauge)

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Condition D starts from the as-received SPCC sheet (same starting state as condition A 'As received'); no pre-strain is applied before the heat treatment. Material is mild steel in which dislocations are locked by carbon and other solutes through the Cottrell effect.

Heat treatment at 373 K for 90 h applied to the as-received material to recover only the Cottrell atmosphere by diffusion of C whilst keeping the dislocations stationary; the condition was calculated from the average diffusion distance of solute C in an Fe matrix, x = (2Dt)^(1/2).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Elastic modulus calculated from the initial stage (strain < 0.1%); value listed for the region of strain 0–0.05%. Stress–strain curve measured with a load cell and strain gauge up to ~1% strain.
Elastic modulus calculated from the whole elastic region (Fig. 4, strain up to 0.3% plotted; modulus from the stress–strain curves within the elastic deformation region).

defects.type: dislocations (locked by carbon/solutes via the Cottrell effect; Cottrell atmosphere recovered and dislocations restrained by the 373 K/90 h heat treatment)

structures.overall_structure: Mild steel (SPCC) with an Fe matrix in which dislocations are locked by carbon and other solutes via the Cottrell effect in the as-received state; the 373 K/90 h heat treatment applied to specimen D recovers the Cottrell atmosphere by C diffusion while keeping the dislocations stationary, thereby restraining the movable dislocations.

unmapped_findings: The nano-indentation experiments (spherical tip, nominal R = 50 μm; Figs 7–12) are described only for 'the specimens' and the marker schematic in Fig. 10 labels the specimen 'SPCE', so these microscopic elastic-modulus results are not attributed to the SPCC species D.

Table 2 and Fig. 4 print no units for the elastic-modulus values; the numbers reported for species D (189 for 0–0.05% strain and 189 for the whole elastic range) are therefore recorded without any unit.

For species D the modulus measured over the narrow 0–0.05% strain window (189) equals that measured over the whole elastic range (189), whereas species A, B and C show a gap between the two ranges (A: 182 vs 173; B: 188 vs 162; C: 186 vs 162).

The 373 K/90 h heat-treatment condition was selected using the average diffusion distance of solute C in an Fe matrix, x = (2Dt)^(1/2), to recover only the Cottrell atmosphere while keeping dislocations stationary.
